note: Record regions, not countries. A region is a piece of ground whose records were filed the same way, and an era is a stretch of years over which that stayed true. The regime bands are the researched sovereignty of the Defranceski archive; what is new here is `filedUnder` — which archive a regime actually MEANS. That is the whole point: knowing Gračišće was Italian in 1930 is trivia until it tells you to open FamilySearch's Pola and Trieste collection rather than its Croatian one.
precision: The rings are approximate — deliberately. They exist to shade which filing system a place fell under, not to adjudicate a border. A place near a ring's edge should be checked against both neighbours.

eras.note: No parish registers exist anywhere for this period. Trent required them only from 1563, and Istria's earliest surviving books are seventeenth-century.
The books stayed with the parish and were gathered to Pazin in the twentieth century. FamilySearch filmed them as Croatia, Church Books (collection 2040054).
The parish books continue unbroken; the regime change is invisible in them.
Parish registers to Pazin. The imperial press covering these years is in ANNO, and it names people the registers only number.

THE TRAP. Records of these years are filed under ITALY, not Croatia — FamilySearch's Italy, Pola and Trieste collection (2152685) holds Croatian parishes. Searching the Croatian collection alone finds nothing.
Civil registration is patchy. Arolsen holds the deportation and forced-labour records of these years.
Registration moves to the matični ured. Anything inside the hundred-year privacy cut-off is not public, whoever holds it.
Current registration is with the matični ured in Pazin. Not public.
Before registers.

eras.polity: Republic of Venice — Istria da Mar
eras.note: Venetian Istria, diocese of Pola. The registers are in Italian and Latin and the hands are Venetian.
Pula becomes the imperial navy's main port, and the population triples. Naval and garrison records are Viennese, not local.
Filed under Italy. FamilySearch collection 2152685 covers Buje, Novigrad, Oprtalj, Brtonigla and Materada among others.
The esodo: most of the Italian-speaking population leaves between 1945 and 1956. People vanish from these registers without dying.

regions.label: The Kvarner — Senj, Vinodol, Rijeka
regions.sub: Rijeka, Bakar, Crikvenica, Novi Vinodolski, Senj

eras.polity: Frankopan counts of Krk and Vinodol
eras.note: Before registers.

eras.polity: Habsburg — Senj a Military Frontier garrison
eras.note: THE TRAP. Senj was Militärgrenze, administered from Vienna and Graz, not from Croatia's civil counties. Military Frontier material is in the Croatian State Archive and in the Vienna Kriegsarchiv — not where a Croatian county search would look.

eras.polity: Austria–Hungary — Fiume a Hungarian corpus separatum
eras.note: THE TRAP. Rijeka/Fiume was governed from BUDAPEST, not Vienna or Zagreb, from 1779. Its administrative records are Hungarian — which is why Hungaricana finds them and Croatian catalogues sometimes do not.
The border ran through the town. Fiume was Italian and Sušak, across the Rječina, was Yugoslav — two filing systems, one city, for twenty-five years.

regions.label: Carnia, Friuli
regions.sub: Ovaro, Mione, Muina, Agrons — the Val Degano

eras.note: Before registers.

eras.polity: Republic of Venice — Patria del Friuli
eras.note: Parish registers only, kept by the parish and now largely with the diocese of Udine. There is no civil registration yet.
THE GOOD NEWS. Civil registration begins in 1806 — births, marriages and deaths recorded by the comune, in Italian, in a standard form. Antenati has the images, free and without an account.
Civil registration lapses; the parish register is the record again for these fifty years.
Civil registration resumes in 1871. Antenati holds Udine's, and FamilySearch filmed the same books as collection 1939238.
Before registers.
Venetian Dalmatia. Many parish books went to Zadar rather than Split, which is where a Split-only search fails.
Governed from Zadar, and its records went there.
A short Italian occupation with its own paperwork, easy to miss between two Yugoslav periods.

regions.label: The Imotski frontier
regions.sub: Imotski and the Zagora — the Venetian-Ottoman border

eras.note: THE HOLE. Two hundred years of Ottoman rule, and Catholic parish registers barely survive it. What exists for these years is Franciscan, held by the monasteries, and almost none of it is online.
Taken by Venice in 1717. Registers begin here, and effectively nowhere earlier.
